sections.Unit: Generic unit metadata, documentation, dependency and ordering information; shared by all unit types (systemd.unit(5)).
sections.Install: How the unit is wired into the boot graph by systemctl enable; consumed by enable/preset operations only (systemd.unit(5)).
sections.Service: Process supervision settings for .service units; also collects the shared exec/kill/resource-control options (systemd.service(5)).
sections.Socket: Socket and FIFO activation settings for .socket units (systemd.socket(5)).
sections.Timer: Calendar and monotonic scheduling settings for .timer units (systemd.timer(5)).
sections.Path: Filesystem path watch triggers for .path units (systemd.path(5)).
sections.Swap: Swap device and file parameters for .swap units (systemd.swap(5)).
sections.Target: Grouping unit that pulls in other units via Wants=/Requires=; has no own section directives (systemd.target(5)).
sections.Device: Unit exposing kernel device state as discovered via udev; has no own section directives (systemd.device(5)).
sections.Slice: Resource-control hierarchy node for process grouping (systemd.slice(5), systemd.resource-control(5)).
sections.Scope: Externally created process group supervised like a service (systemd.scope(5)).

Unit.Description: Short human-readable title for the unit, shown in systemctl status output and journal headers.
Unit.Documentation: Space-separated URIs (man:, https:, file:) pointing to documentation for this unit; shown by systemctl help.
Unit.Wants: Weak requirements; listed units are started together with this one, but their failure does not affect this unit.
Unit.Requires: Hard requirements; if a listed unit fails to activate, this unit will not be started.
Unit.Requisite: If a listed unit is not already active, this unit fails immediately instead of pulling it in.
Unit.BindsTo: When combined with After=, this unit is stopped whenever any listed unit becomes inactive.
Unit.PartOf: When the listed unit is stopped or restarted, this unit is stopped or restarted as well.
Unit.Upholds: Listed units are kept continuously active while this unit is active; if they stop unexpectedly they are restarted.
Unit.Conflicts: Reverse dependency; activating this unit stops the listed units, and activating them stops this unit.
Unit.Before: Ordering dependency; this unit is started before the listed units (and stopped after them).
Unit.After: Ordering dependency; this unit is started after the listed units (and stopped before them).
Unit.OnFailure: Units activated when this unit enters the failed state.
Unit.OnSuccess: Units activated when this unit enters the inactive state after succeeding.
Unit.PropagatesReloadTo: Reload requests made to this unit are propagated to the listed units.
Unit.ReloadPropagatedFrom: Reload requests made to the listed units are propagated to this unit.
Unit.PropagatesStopTo: Stop requests made to this unit are propagated to the listed units.
Unit.StopPropagatedFrom: Stop requests made to the listed units are propagated to this unit.
Unit.JoinsNamespaceOf: Shares filesystem, network or IPC namespaces set up via Private*= directives with the listed units.
Unit.RequiresMountsFor: Adds Requires= and After= dependencies on the mount units backing the listed absolute paths.
Unit.OnFailureJobMode: Job mode used when pulling in OnFailure= units (default fail).
Unit.OnSuccessJobMode: Job mode used when pulling in OnSuccess= units (default fail).
Unit.IgnoreOnIsolate: If true, this unit is not stopped when another unit is isolated via systemctl isolate.
Unit.StopWhenUnneeded: If true, the unit is stopped automatically when no other active unit Wants= or Requires= it.
Unit.RefuseManualStart: If true, the unit can only be started as a dependency, refusing direct systemctl start.
Unit.RefuseManualStop: If true, the unit can only be stopped as a side effect of dependencies, refusing direct systemctl stop.
Unit.AllowIsolate: If true, the unit may be used with systemctl isolate (default false).
Unit.DefaultDependencies: If true (default), adds basic ordering dependencies such as sysinit.target and shutdown.target.
Unit.CollectMode: Controls when the unit runtime state is garbage-collected after becoming inactive: inactive or active.
Unit.FailureAction: Action to take when the unit enters the failed state: none, reboot, poweroff, exit and -force/-immediate variants.
Unit.SuccessAction: Action to take when the unit succeeds: none, reboot, poweroff, exit and -force/-immediate variants.
Unit.FailureActionExitStatus: Exit status to report for the exit action triggered by FailureAction=.
Unit.SuccessActionExitStatus: Exit status to report for the exit action triggered by SuccessAction=.
Unit.JobTimeoutSec: Maximum time jobs (start/stop) for this unit may take; infinity disables the timeout.
Unit.JobRunningTimeoutSec: Maximum time a successfully activated unit may keep its job in the running state.
Unit.JobTimeoutAction: Action to take when the job timeout is hit (same vocabulary as FailureAction=).
Unit.JobTimeoutRebootArgument: Optional argument passed to the reboot() system call for the reboot actions.
Unit.StartLimitIntervalSec: Configures the rate-limiting window used together with StartLimitBurst= (default 10s).
Unit.StartLimitBurst: Number of start attempts allowed within StartLimitIntervalSec= before the unit fails to start (default 5).
Unit.StartLimitAction: Action taken when the start rate limit is hit (default none).
Unit.RebootArgument: Optional argument passed to the reboot() system call for reboot actions of this unit.
Unit.SourcePath: Deprecated; the path of the configuration file this unit was generated from.
Unit.ConditionPathExists: Condition: the given absolute path exists; otherwise the unit is skipped (condition failure is not an error).
Unit.ConditionPathIsDirectory: Condition: the given path exists and is a directory.
Unit.ConditionPathIsSymbolicLink: Condition: the given path exists and is a symbolic link.
Unit.ConditionPathIsMountPoint: Condition: the given path is a mount point.
Unit.ConditionPathIsReadWrite: Condition: the given path exists and is readable and writable.
Unit.ConditionPathExistsGlob: Condition: at least one file matching the given glob expression exists.
Unit.ConditionDirectoryNotEmpty: Condition: the given directory exists and contains at least one file.
Unit.ConditionFileNotEmpty: Condition: the given file exists and has a size greater than zero.
Unit.ConditionFileIsExecutable: Condition: the given file exists and is executable by this unit's user.
Unit.ConditionUser: Condition: the user (name or UID, or @system for any system user) matches the one the manager runs as.
Unit.ConditionGroup: Condition: the group (name or GID) of the manager matches the argument.
Unit.ConditionHost: Condition: the hostname or machine ID matches the argument.
Unit.ConditionKernelCommandLine: Condition: the given kernel command line option (optionally with =value) is set.
Unit.ConditionKernelVersion: Condition: the kernel version matches the given glob expression.
Unit.ConditionArchitecture: Condition: the system architecture matches (x86-64, aarch64, and so on).
Unit.ConditionVirtualization: Condition: virtualization status matches (yes, no, vm, container, qemu, kvm, and so on).
Unit.ConditionSecurity: Condition: the given security module (selinux, apparmor, ima, and so on) is enabled.
Unit.ConditionCapability: Condition: the given capability (CAP_*) is available in the capability bounding set.
Unit.ConditionACPower: Condition: true or false depending on whether the system runs on AC power.
Unit.ConditionNeedsUpdate: Condition: the given directory (/etc or /var) needs an update according to its .updated stamps.
Unit.ConditionFirstBoot: Condition: true on the first boot after an OS installation or upgrade.
Unit.ConditionMemory: Condition: total system memory is at least the given byte value (K/M/G/T suffixes allowed).
Unit.ConditionCPUs: Condition: the system has at least the given number of CPUs.
Unit.ConditionEnvironment: Condition: the given environment variable is set (optionally to a specific value).
Unit.ConditionControlGroupController: Condition: the given cgroup controller (cpu, io, memory, and so on) is available.
Unit.AssertPathExists: Assertion: the given path exists; if not, starting the unit fails (assertion failure is a hard error).
Unit.AssertFileNotEmpty: Assertion: the given file exists and has a size greater than zero.
Unit.AssertFileIsExecutable: Assertion: the given file exists and is executable.
Unit.AssertUser: Assertion: the user the manager runs as matches the argument.
Unit.AssertGroup: Assertion: the group of the manager matches the argument.
Unit.AssertHost: Assertion: the hostname or machine ID matches the argument.
Unit.AssertVirtualization: Assertion: virtualization status matches (same vocabulary as ConditionVirtualization=).
Unit.AssertACPower: Assertion: the system is (or is not) running on AC power.
Unit.AssertKernelCommandLine: Assertion: the given kernel command line option is set.
Unit.AssertArchitecture: Assertion: the system architecture matches the argument.

Install.Alias: Additional names the unit is installed as (for example display-manager.service as an alias of a display manager unit).
Install.WantedBy: Installs a Wants= dependency from the listed units to this unit; systemctl enable symlinks into their .wants/ directories.
Install.RequiredBy: Installs a Requires= dependency from the listed units to this unit (.requires/ directories).
Install.UpheldBy: Installs an Upholds= dependency from the listed units to this unit (.upholds/ directories).
Install.Also: Additional units to enable or disable together with this unit.
Install.DefaultInstance: Default instance name used when enabling a template unit without an explicit instance.

Service.Type: Process start-up type: how the main process is created and when the service counts as started (simple, exec, forking, oneshot, notify, dbus, idle).
Service.ExitType: Determines which process is considered the main one for exit status purposes: main, cgroup or mixed.
Service.RemainAfterExit: If true, the service stays active after the main process exits (typically combined with Type=oneshot).
Service.GuessMainPID: If true, systemd guesses the main PID for Type=forking when no PIDFile= is set (default true).
Service.PIDFile: Path to a PID file containing the main PID, used with Type=forking to avoid guessing.
Service.BusName: D-Bus bus name the service acquires; used with Type=dbus as the readiness criterion.
Service.ExecStart: Command with arguments run when the unit is started; supports the prefixes -, +, :, ! and !! to tweak failure, privileges and expansion.
Service.ExecStartPre: Commands run before ExecStart=, usually setup or sanity checks; prefix with - to ignore failure.
Service.ExecStartPost: Commands run after the service is started, subject to the Type= readiness semantics.
Service.ExecCondition: Command run before ExecStart=; a nonzero exit skips the start and is treated like a failed condition, not a failure.
Service.ExecReload: Command executed on systemctl reload; commonly /bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID or a binary reload trigger.
Service.ExecStop: Command executed on systemctl stop; remaining processes are killed afterwards per KillMode=.
Service.ExecStopPost: Commands run after the service has stopped, regardless of success or failure (cleanup).
Service.RestartSec: Time to sleep before restarting the service (default 100ms).
Service.TimeoutStartSec: Maximum time to wait for the start to finish; infinity disables it (manager default 90s).
Service.TimeoutStopSec: Maximum time to wait for the stop to finish; infinity disables it (manager default 90s).
Service.TimeoutSec: Shorthand that sets both TimeoutStartSec= and TimeoutStopSec=.
Service.TimeoutAbortSec: Maximum time to wait for the service to terminate after a crash before SIGKILL is sent.
Service.TimeoutStartFailureMode: What to do when TimeoutStartSec= is hit: exit, abort (core dump) or kill.
Service.TimeoutStopFailureMode: What to do when TimeoutStopSec= is hit: exit, abort or kill (default kill via SIGKILL).
Service.RuntimeMaxSec: Maximum time the service may run; on expiry it is terminated and, subject to Restart=, not restarted.
Service.RuntimeRandomizedExtraSec: Extra randomized delay added to RuntimeMaxSec= (uniform between 0 and the value).
Service.WatchdogSec: Enables the service watchdog with the given timeout; the service must call sd_notify('WATCHDOG=1') to stay alive.
Service.Restart: When to restart the service: no, on-success, on-failure, on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort or always.
Service.SuccessExitStatus: Exit statuses (or signal names) that count as successful termination for Restart= logic.
Service.RestartPreventExitStatus: Exit statuses that never trigger a restart, taking precedence over RestartForceExitStatus=.
Service.RestartForceExitStatus: Exit statuses that always trigger a restart, overriding Restart=.
Service.RootDirectoryStartOnly: If true, only ExecStart= runs inside RootDirectory=, while the pre/post commands keep the full root view.
Service.NonBlocking: If true, the socket passed to a socket-activated service is set to non-blocking mode.
Service.NotifyAccess: Which processes may send sd_notify() notifications: none, main, exec or all (default main).
Service.OOMPolicy: What to do when the kernel OOM killer kills a process of the unit: continue, stop or kill.
Service.WorkingDirectory: Changes to this directory before ExecStart=; prefix with - to skip when the directory is missing.
Service.RootDirectory: Chroots executed processes into the given directory (see RootImage= for image based alternatives).
Service.RootImage: Mounts the given OS image as the root filesystem for the service processes.
Service.MountAPIVFS: If true, mounts /proc, /sys and /dev inside the service's RootDirectory= or RootImage=.
Service.ProtectProc: Restricts visibility of /proc entries: noaccess, invisible, ptraceable or default.
Service.ProcSubset: Restricts /proc to a subset: all (default) or pid (only processes of the unit).
Service.User: Unix user the processes are executed as (or a user@.service instance for template units).
Service.Group: Unix group the processes are executed as.
Service.SupplementaryGroups: Additional Unix groups the processes are made a member of.
Service.DynamicUser: If true, a transient user and group are allocated for the service at runtime (implies several hardening defaults).
Service.PAMName: Sets up the processes as a PAM session with the given name (requires root).
Service.CapabilityBoundingSet: Caps the capabilities available to the processes; an empty value drops all, a ~ prefix removes listed ones (e.g. CAP_NET_ADMIN).
Service.AmbientCapabilities: Adds capabilities to the effective set beyond the inherited ones, e.g. CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE.
Service.NoNewPrivileges: If true, the processes and their children can never gain privileges via setuid/setgid bits or file capabilities.
Service.SecureBits: Linux secure bits (keep-caps, no-setuid-fixup, noroot and their locked variants).
Service.SELinuxContext: Sets the SELinux security context for the processes (or reset).
Service.AppArmorProfile: Sets the AppArmor profile for the processes (or unconfined).
Service.SmackProcessLabel: Sets the SMACK label for the processes.
Service.LimitCPU: CPU time limit (ulimit -t equivalent), e.g. 10min or infinity.
Service.LimitFSIZE: Maximum size of files created by the processes, e.g. 100M or infinity.
Service.LimitDATA: Maximum data segment size, e.g. 1G or infinity.
Service.LimitSTACK: Maximum stack size, e.g. 8M or infinity.
Service.LimitCORE: Maximum core dump file size; 0 disables core dumps, infinity removes the limit.
Service.LimitRSS: Maximum resident set size (mostly a no-op on current Linux kernels).
Service.LimitNOFILE: Maximum number of open file descriptors, e.g. 16384 or infinity.
Service.LimitAS: Maximum address space (virtual memory), e.g. 2G or infinity.
Service.LimitNPROC: Maximum number of processes for the user (ulimit -u).
Service.LimitMSGQUEUE: Maximum bytes in POSIX message queues (ulimit -q).
Service.LimitNICE: Nice level ceiling shift (ulimit -e); typical values 0-40.
Service.LimitRTTIME: Maximum real-time CPU time for realtime processes (us, ms, s suffixes).
Service.UMask: File mode creation mask for the processes, e.g. 0027.
Service.KeyringMode: Kernel session keyring handling: private (new session keyring, default), shared or inherit.
Service.OOMScoreAdjust: Adjusts the OOM killer bias from -1000 to +1000; higher values mean the unit is killed sooner.
Service.TimerSlackNSec: Sets the timer slack for the processes in nanoseconds (default 50us).
Service.Personality: Controls the syscall ABI personality of the processes, e.g. x86 on an x86-64 kernel.
Service.IgnoreSIGPIPE: If true (default), SIGPIPE is reset to default (ignored) for the processes.
Service.Nice: Sets the nice level from -20 to 19 for the processes.
Service.CPUSchedulingPolicy: CPU scheduling class: other, batch, idle, fifo or rr.
Service.CPUSchedulingPriority: Static priority for the realtime policies fifo and rr (1-99).
Service.CPUSchedulingResetOnFork: If true, the scheduling policy and priority reset to the defaults on fork().
Service.CPUAffinity: Pins the processes to the listed CPU indices or ranges; may be listed multiple times.
Service.NUMAPolicy: NUMA memory policy: default, bind, interleave, preferred, local or mbind.
Service.NUMAMask: NUMA node mask used by NUMAPolicy=.
Service.IOSchedulingClass: I/O scheduling class: none, realtime, best-effort or idle.
Service.IOSchedulingPriority: I/O scheduling priority from 0 (highest) to 7 for the realtime and best-effort classes.
Service.ProtectSystem: Read-only protection for the filesystem hierarchy: no, yes (/usr, /boot, /efi), full (plus /etc) or strict (everything except device and API filesystems).
Service.ProtectHome: Access control for /home, /root and /run/user: no, yes (inaccessible), read-only or tmpfs.
Service.ReadWritePaths: Whitelists the listed paths as writable even under ProtectSystem= strict or ReadOnlyPaths=.
Service.ReadOnlyPaths: Makes the listed paths and their submounts read-only.
Service.InaccessiblePaths: Makes the listed paths inaccessible by mounting empty files over them.
Service.ExecPaths: Whitelists the listed paths as the only ones allowing execution (combined with NoExecPaths=).
Service.NoExecPaths: Forbids execution of files under the listed paths.
Service.PrivateTmp: If true, the service gets its own private /tmp and /var/tmp namespaces.
Service.PrivateDevices: If true, the service sees only private pseudo devices in /dev (no physical device access).
Service.PrivateNetwork: If true, the service gets its own network namespace with only the loopback device.
Service.PrivateIPC: If true, the service gets its own IPC namespace (POSIX message queues, semaphores, shared memory).
Service.PrivateUsers: If true, runs the processes with an unprivileged user namespace UID mapping.
Service.PrivateMounts: If true, the service gets its own private mount namespace.
Service.ProtectHostname: If true, the processes cannot change the hostname or domainname (UTS namespace).
Service.ProtectClock: If true, the processes cannot change the system clock (CAP_SYS_TIME and RTK device access dropped).
Service.ProtectKernelTunables: If true, /proc/sys, /sys and kernel module parameters become read-only.
Service.ProtectKernelModules: If true, the processes cannot load or unload kernel modules.
Service.ProtectKernelLogs: If true, access to kernel logs (dmesg, /dev/kmsg) is denied.
Service.ProtectControlGroups: If true, the cgroup hierarchy becomes read-only for the processes.
Service.RestrictAddressFamilies: Whitelists socket address families: AF_UNIX, AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_NETLINK, or none.
Service.RestrictNamespaces: Forbids creating namespaces of the listed types (mnt, net, pid, ...) or all.
Service.RestrictRealtime: If true, realtime scheduling is denied (protects against RT lockups by unprivileged services).
Service.RestrictSUIDSGID: If true, creation of setuid and setgid files is denied.
Service.RestrictFileSystems: Whitelists filesystem types the unit may access by mounting, e.g. ext4 tmpfs; ~ prefix denies listed ones.
Service.RemoveIPC: If true, System V and POSIX IPC objects owned by the unit's user are removed when it stops.
Service.MemoryDenyWriteExecute: If true, memory mappings cannot be both writable and executable.
Service.LockPersonality: If true, the processes cannot switch their execution domain or personality.
Service.SystemCallFilter: Syscall allow and deny lists, e.g. ~@clock or @system-service; the ~ prefix turns the list into a deny list.
Service.SystemCallErrorNumber: Error number returned to denied syscalls (default ENOSYS), e.g. EPERM.
Service.SystemCallArchitectures: Restricts the syscall ABIs to the listed architectures, e.g. native.
Service.SystemCallLog: Syscalls (names or @groups) to log whenever the processes execute them.
Service.Environment: Sets environment variables for the executed processes; may be listed multiple times.
Service.EnvironmentFile: Reads environment variables from the given file; prefix with - to ignore a missing file.
Service.PassEnvironment: Passes the listed manager environment variables to the processes (by default none are passed).
Service.UnsetEnvironment: Removes the listed variables from the environment seen by the processes.
Service.StandardInput: Connects stdin to null, a tty, the activation socket, a passed fd, inline text or a file.
Service.StandardOutput: Connects stdout to inherit, null, tty, journal (default), kmsg, console variants, the socket, a fd or a file.
Service.StandardError: Connects stderr with the same vocabulary as StandardOutput= (default journal).
Service.LogLevelMax: Filters log messages generated by the service to at most this level: emerg to debug.
Service.LogExtraFields: Attaches extra metadata fields to all log records generated by the unit.
Service.LogRateLimitIntervalSec: Rate limit window for log messages generated by the service (manager default 30s).
Service.LogRateLimitBurst: Number of messages allowed per LogRateLimitIntervalSec= before dropping (manager default 100).
Service.LogNamespace: Runs the service with its own journal namespace instead of the system journal.
Service.SyslogIdentifier: Sets the syslog identifier (SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER) for logged messages (default unit name).
Service.SyslogFacility: Syslog facility for the service messages: kern through local7 (default daemon).
Service.SyslogLevel: Default syslog level for messages: emerg through debug (default info).
Service.SyslogLevelPrefix: If true (default), angle-bracket priority prefixes in logged lines are parsed and stripped.
Service.TTYPath: Sets the TTY device path used when StandardInput= or StandardOutput= is tty.
Service.TTYReset: If true, the TTY is reset before the service starts.
Service.TTYVHangup: If true, all processes on the selected TTY receive SIGHUP before the service starts.
Service.TTYVTDisallocate: If true, the virtual terminal of the TTY is deallocated after the service stops.
Service.TTYColumns: Overrides the TTY column width reported to the service.
Service.TTYRows: Overrides the TTY row height reported to the service.
Service.KillMode: Which processes are killed when the unit stops: control-group (default), process, mixed, user or none.
Service.KillSignal: Signal sent to remaining processes at stop (default SIGTERM).
Service.SendSIGHUP: If true, remaining processes receive SIGHUP right after the SIGTERM signal.
Service.SendSIGKILL: If true (default), SIGKILL is sent to remaining processes after the stop timeout expires.
Service.CPUAccounting: If true, CPU usage of the unit's cgroup is accounted (implicit when a CPU limit is set).
Service.CPUWeight: CPU time share weight from 1 to 10000 (default 100); higher gets more CPU under contention.
Service.StartupCPUWeight: CPU weight applied only while the system is booting up.
Service.CPUQuota: Caps CPU usage, e.g. 20% (a fifth of one core) or 200% (two cores); infinity removes the cap.
Service.CPUQuotaPeriodSec: Duration of the CPU quota period (default 100ms).
Service.AllowedCPUs: Restricts the unit to the listed CPU indices or ranges.
Service.AllowedMemoryNodes: Restricts the unit to the listed NUMA memory nodes.
Service.MemoryAccounting: If true, memory usage of the unit's cgroup is accounted.
Service.MemoryMin: Hard memory protection: this much memory is never considered reclaimable from the unit.
Service.MemoryLow: Soft memory protection: best-effort retention of this much memory under pressure.
Service.MemoryHigh: Throttle point: above this the unit's allocations are strongly reclaimed and slowed.
Service.MemoryMax: Hard limit: allocation beyond this triggers the OOM killer inside the cgroup; infinity removes the limit.
Service.MemorySwapMax: Hard limit on swap usage by the unit; infinity removes the limit.
Service.TasksAccounting: If true, the number of tasks in the unit's cgroup is accounted.
Service.TasksMax: Maximum number of tasks (processes and threads) in the unit; infinity or percentages allowed.
Service.IPAccounting: If true, IPv4 and IPv6 traffic of the unit's processes is accounted.
Service.IPAddressAllow: Whitelists the IP prefixes the unit may talk to; combined with IPAddressDeny=.
Service.IPAddressDeny: Blacklists the IP prefixes the unit may talk to; any matches all addresses.
Service.DevicePolicy: Device node access policy: closed (default), strict (only DeviceAllow= entries) or auto.
Service.DeviceAllow: Whitelists device nodes with rwm access, e.g. /dev/sda, char-usb_device or /dev/loop-control.
Service.Slice: Places the unit in the named slice (default system.slice for system services).
Service.Delegate: Hands the listed cgroup controllers (or all of them) to the unit's manager process; yes, no or a list.
Service.DisableControllers: Disables the listed controllers for the unit's subtree.
Service.IOAccounting: If true, block I/O usage of the unit's cgroup is accounted.
Service.StartupIOWeight: Block I/O weight applied only while the system is booting up.
Service.IOReadBandwidthMax: Caps read throughput, e.g. /dev/sda 5M or just 5M for all devices.
Service.IOWriteBandwidthMax: Caps write throughput, e.g. /dev/sda 5M or just 5M for all devices.
Service.IOReadIOPSMax: Caps read operations per second, per device or globally.
Service.IOWriteIOPSMax: Caps write operations per second, per device or globally.
Service.IODeviceLatencyTargetSec: Sets a latency target with percentile, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1 target=25ms percentile=99%.

Socket.ListenStream: Listens on the given TCP port, AF_UNIX socket path or AF_VSOCK port; may be listed multiple times.
Socket.ListenDatagram: Listens on the given UDP port or AF_UNIX datagram socket path.
Socket.ListenSequentialPacket: Listens on the given sequential packet socket path.
Socket.ListenFIFO: Listens on the given FIFO path in the filesystem.
Socket.ListenSpecial: Listens on the given special file such as /proc/keys.
Socket.ListenMessageQueue: Listens on the given POSIX message queue.
Socket.ListenUSBFunction: Listens on USB gadget functionfs endpoints.
Socket.SocketProtocol: Protocol identifier for special protocols such as udplite or sctp.
Socket.BindIPv6Only: Controls IPV6_V6ONLY for TCP sockets: default, both or ipv6-only.
Socket.Backlog: Listen backlog for the sockets (default is the kernel maximum).
Socket.BindToDevice: Binds the sockets to the given network interface (SO_BINDTODEVICE).
Socket.SocketUser: Owns created socket or FIFO files as this user (name or UID).
Socket.SocketGroup: Owns created socket or FIFO files as this group (name or GID).
Socket.SocketMode: Access mode for created socket or FIFO files, e.g. 0666.
Socket.DirectoryMode: Access mode for parent directories auto-created for the sockets.
Socket.Accept: If true, a service instance is spawned per accepted connection; if false the listener is passed as fd 3.
Socket.Writable: If true, the FIFO is opened writable so the service can write back (bidirectional).
Socket.MaxConnections: Maximum number of concurrently connected clients for Accept= sockets (default 64).
Socket.MaxConnectionsPerSource: Maximum number of concurrent connections from a single client IP.
Socket.KeepAlive: If true, TCP keep-alive is enabled for accepted sockets.
Socket.KeepAliveTimeSec: Idle time before the first keep-alive probe is sent.
Socket.KeepAliveProbes: Number of lost probes before the connection is declared dead.
Socket.NoDelay: If true, TCP_NODELAY is enabled on accepted sockets.
Socket.Priority: Socket priority value used for QoS (SO_PRIORITY).
Socket.DeferAcceptSec: Waits for data before passing an accepted TCP socket to the service (TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT).
Socket.ReceiveBuffer: Receive buffer size for the sockets (SO_RCVBUF), e.g. 1M.
Socket.SendBuffer: Send buffer size for the sockets (SO_SNDBUF), e.g. 1M.
Socket.IPTOS: IP Type-of-Service value for packets sent on the sockets.
Socket.IPTTL: IP Time-To-Live for outgoing unicast packets.
Socket.Mark: Firewall mark set on packets generated by the sockets (SO_MARK).
Socket.ReusePort: If true, SO_REUSEPORT allows multiple sockets to bind the same port.
Socket.SmackLabel: SMACK label set on the sockets.
Socket.SELinuxContextFromNet: If true, the SELinux context of the connection is taken from the network peer.
Socket.FreeBind: If true, binding to non-local addresses is allowed (IP_FREEBIND) for failover setups.
Socket.Transparent: If true, IP_TRANSPARENT is enabled for proxying setups.
Socket.Broadcast: If true, SO_BROADCAST is enabled on datagram sockets.
Socket.PassCredentials: If true, SCM_CREDENTIALS ancillary data is passed on the sockets (SO_PASSCRED).
Socket.PassSecurity: If true, the peer's security label is passed (SO_PASSSEC).
Socket.PassPacketInfo: If true, ancillary packet information is passed (IP_PKTINFO / IPV6_RECVPKTINFO).
Socket.TCPCongestion: TCP congestion control algorithm for the sockets, e.g. bbr or cubic.
Socket.ExecStartPre: Commands run before the socket is created; prefix with - to ignore failure.
Socket.ExecStartPost: Commands run after the socket or listener is set up.
Socket.ExecStopPost: Commands run after the socket is torn down, regardless of success.
Socket.TimeoutSec: Time to wait for the ExecStartPre/Post commands to finish (manager default 90s).
Socket.Service: The service unit to activate on incoming traffic (defaults to the same-named .service unit).
Socket.RemoveOnStop: If true, created socket and FIFO files are removed when the socket unit stops.
Socket.Symlinks: Creates symlinks to the socket at the listed paths.
Socket.FileDescriptorName: Name for the listener fd passed to the service (FDNAME in sd_listen_fds).
Socket.TriggerLimitIntervalSec: Rate limit window for activation triggers (default 2s).
Socket.TriggerLimitBurst: Activations allowed per TriggerLimitIntervalSec= before the unit fails (default 200).

Timer.OnActiveSec: Monotonic timer: elapses this much time after the timer unit itself is activated.
Timer.OnBootSec: Monotonic timer: elapses this much time after the system booted.
Timer.OnStartupSec: Monotonic timer: elapses this much time after the service manager started.
Timer.OnUnitActiveSec: Monotonic timer: elapses this much time after the last activation of the unit being activated.
Timer.OnUnitInactiveSec: Monotonic timer: elapses this much time after the last deactivation of the unit being activated.
Timer.OnCalendar: Calendar event expression such as Mon..Fri 09:00, weekly, *:0/15 or UTC 02:00 (systemd.time(7)).
Timer.OnClockChange: If true, the timer triggers when the system clock jumps (CLOCK_REALTIME change).
Timer.OnTimezoneChange: If true, the timer triggers when the local timezone changes.
Timer.AccuracySec: Window the elapse may be deferred into for batching (default 1min; smaller means more wakeups).
Timer.RandomizedDelaySec: Randomly delays each elapse by up to this much (default 0).
Timer.FixedRandomDelay: If true, a fixed random offset is used instead of rolling a new one each time.
Timer.Persistent: If true, an elapse missed while the unit was inactive triggers at the next opportunity.
Timer.WakeSystem: If true, the timer elapse wakes the system from suspend.
Timer.RemainAfterElapse: If true (default), the timer stays active after elapsing once (irrelevant for repeating timers).
Timer.Unit: The unit to activate; defaults to the same-named .service unit.

Mount.What: The device or resource to mount, e.g. /dev/sda1, tmpfs or //server/share.
Mount.Where: The absolute mount point path; must match the encoded unit filename.
Mount.Type: The filesystem type, e.g. ext4, nfs4 or cifs.
Mount.Options: Mount options passed to mount(8), comma separated.
Mount.SloppyOptions: If true, unsupported options are ignored by the mount helper (mount -s, for NFS).
Mount.LazyUnmount: If true, the mount is detached from the tree at stop (MNT_DETACH, umount -l).
Mount.ForceUnmount: If true, the unmount is forced at stop even when busy (umount -f).
Mount.ReadWriteOnly: If true, the mount fails instead of falling back to read-only when write support is missing.
Mount.DirectoryMode: Access mode for the auto-created mount point directory.
Mount.TimeoutSec: How long to wait for the mount command to finish (manager default 90s).

Automount.Where: The mount point path to automount; must match the encoded unit filename.
Automount.DirectoryMode: Access mode for the auto-created mount point directory.
Automount.TimeoutIdleSec: Unmounts the mounted filesystem after being idle this long; infinity disables it.

Path.PathExists: Triggers when the given path exists.
Path.PathExistsGlob: Triggers when at least one file matching the glob expression exists.
Path.PathChanged: Triggers when the given path or a watched file changes (after writes settle).
Path.PathModified: Triggers on every change of the path's contents (may fire repeatedly during writes).
Path.DirectoryNotEmpty: Triggers when the given directory contains at least one file.
Path.Unit: The unit to activate; defaults to the same-named .service unit.
Path.MakeDirectory: If true, the watched directory is created when missing.
Path.TriggerLimitIntervalSec: Rate limit window for path activation triggers (default 2s).
Path.TriggerLimitBurst: Activations allowed per TriggerLimitIntervalSec= before the unit fails (default 200).

Swap.What: The swap device or swap file to activate.
Swap.Priority: Swap priority used at swapon; -1 lets the kernel pick.
Swap.Options: Swap activation options passed to swapon(8).
Swap.TimeoutSec: How long to wait for swapon to finish (manager default 90s).

Slice.CPUAccounting: If true, CPU usage of the slice's cgroup is accounted.
Slice.CPUWeight: CPU time share weight from 1 to 10000 (default 100); higher gets more CPU under contention.
Slice.StartupCPUWeight: CPU weight applied only while the system is booting up.
Slice.CPUQuota: Caps CPU usage, e.g. 20% or 200%; infinity removes the cap.
Slice.AllowedCPUs: Restricts the slice to the listed CPU indices or ranges.
Slice.MemoryAccounting: If true, memory usage of the slice's cgroup is accounted.
Slice.MemoryMin: Hard memory protection: this much memory is never considered reclaimable from the slice.
Slice.MemoryLow: Soft memory protection: best-effort retention of this much memory under pressure.
Slice.MemoryHigh: Throttle point: above this the slice's allocations are strongly reclaimed and slowed.
Slice.MemoryMax: Hard limit: allocation beyond this triggers the OOM killer inside the cgroup.
Slice.MemorySwapMax: Hard limit on swap usage by the slice; infinity removes the limit.
Slice.TasksAccounting: If true, the number of tasks in the slice's cgroup is accounted.
Slice.TasksMax: Maximum number of tasks in the slice; infinity or percentages allowed.
Slice.DevicePolicy: Device node access policy: closed (default), strict or auto.
Slice.DeviceAllow: Whitelists device nodes with rwm access.
Slice.Delegate: Hands the listed cgroup controllers (or all) to the slice's owner process; yes, no or a list.
Slice.DisableControllers: Disables the listed controllers for the slice's subtree.
Slice.IOAccounting: If true, block I/O usage of the slice's cgroup is accounted.
Slice.IOReadBandwidthMax: Caps read throughput, per device or globally.
Slice.IOWriteBandwidthMax: Caps write throughput, per device or globally.

Scope.TimeoutStopSec: Maximum time to wait for the scope to stop; infinity disables the timeout.
Scope.RuntimeMaxSec: Maximum time the scope may run before it is terminated.
Scope.KillMode: Which processes are killed when the scope stops: control-group (default), process, mixed, user or none.
Scope.KillSignal: Signal sent to remaining processes at stop (default SIGTERM).
Scope.SendSIGHUP: If true, remaining processes receive SIGHUP right after the SIGTERM signal.
Scope.SendSIGKILL: If true (default), SIGKILL is sent to remaining processes after the stop timeout.
Scope.Slice: Places the scope in the named slice (default system.slice for system scopes).
Scope.Delegate: Hands the listed cgroup controllers (or all) to the scope's leader process.
Scope.TasksMax: Maximum number of tasks in the scope; infinity or percentages allowed.
Scope.MemoryMax: Hard memory limit for the scope; allocation beyond this triggers the OOM killer.

CollectMode.inactive: Runtime state is garbage-collected when the unit becomes inactive (default).
CollectMode.active: Runtime state stays around until the unit is reset or the manager restarts.

FailureAction.reboot-force: Force an immediate reboot without stopping units cleanly.
FailureAction.reboot-immediate: Immediate reboot via the reboot() syscall.
FailureAction.poweroff: Power off normally after a shutdown.
FailureAction.exit: Exit the manager (default for user units).

SuccessAction.reboot-force: Force an immediate reboot without stopping units cleanly.
SuccessAction.reboot-immediate: Immediate reboot via the reboot() syscall.
SuccessAction.poweroff: Power off normally after a shutdown.
SuccessAction.exit: Exit the manager (default for user units).

StartLimitAction.none: No action beyond refusing to start the unit (default).
StartLimitAction.reboot-immediate: Immediate reboot via the reboot() syscall.
StartLimitAction.poweroff: Power off normally after a shutdown.

OnFailureJobMode.replace-irreversibly: Replace jobs and forbid cancelling them again.
OnFailureJobMode.isolate: Stop all other units and start this one.
OnFailureJobMode.flush: Drop all queued jobs and run this one.

OnSuccessJobMode.replace-irreversibly: Replace jobs and forbid cancelling them again.
OnSuccessJobMode.isolate: Stop all other units and start this one.
OnSuccessJobMode.flush: Drop all queued jobs and run this one.

Type.simple: The ExecStart= process is the main process; the service is considered started immediately (default).
Type.exec: Like simple, but the service counts as started once the main process has fully executed.
Type.forking: The process forks a daemon and exits; systemd tracks the child via PIDFile= or guessing.
Type.oneshot: Like simple, but the service finishes when the main process exits; no restarts unless Restart= is set.
Type.notify: Like exec, but the service must call sd_notify('READY=1') to signal readiness.
Type.notify-reload: Like notify, plus sd_notify('RELOADING=1/READY=1') style reload signaling support.
Type.dbus: Like simple, but readiness is acquiring the D-Bus name set in BusName=.
Type.idle: Like simple, but execution is delayed until other dispatched jobs settle.

ExitType.main: Only the main process determines the exit status (default).
ExitType.cgroup: Any process left in the cgroup keeps the service alive and determines the result.
ExitType.mixed: The main process determines the exit status; remaining cgroup processes are killed.

Restart.on-success: Restart only when it exits cleanly (zero or SuccessExitStatus=).
Restart.on-failure: Restart when it exits uncleanly, is killed or times out.
Restart.on-abnormal: Restart when killed by a signal or a timeout, not on unclean exit.
Restart.on-watchdog: Restart only when the watchdog expires.
Restart.on-abort: Restart when the process dies from an unclean signal.
Restart.always: Restart regardless of the exit reason (even when stopped cleanly).

KillMode.control-group: All remaining processes in the control group are killed (default, recommended).
KillMode.process: Only the main process is killed.
KillMode.mixed: The main process gets SIGTERM; all remaining processes get SIGKILL.
KillMode.user: All processes of the user the unit runs as are killed.
KillMode.none: No process is killed (dangerous, leaves leftovers).

NotifyAccess.main: Only the main process may notify (default).
NotifyAccess.exec: The main process and all ExecStart= spawned processes may notify.
NotifyAccess.all: All processes of the unit may notify.

OOMPolicy.continue: Keep the unit running when the kernel OOM killer strikes (default for services).
OOMPolicy.stop: Stop the unit when the OOM killer kills one of its processes.
OOMPolicy.kill: Kill all remaining processes of the cgroup.

StandardInput.tty: Connect the TTY from TTYPath=; fail if unavailable.
StandardInput.tty-fail: Connect the controlling TTY, failing the unit if there is none.
StandardInput.tty-escape: Like tty, but the TTY is only used while the process runs.
StandardInput.fd: Connect a file descriptor passed to the manager (FDSTORE).

StandardOutput.inherit: Duplicate the journal file descriptors of the manager.
StandardOutput.tty: Write to the TTY from TTYPath=.
StandardOutput.journal: Write to the journal (default), tagged with the unit metadata.
StandardOutput.kmsg: Write to the kernel log buffer (/dev/kmsg).
StandardOutput.kmsg+console: Kernel log buffer plus the console.
StandardOutput.fd: Write to a file descriptor passed to the manager.

StandardError.tty: Write to the TTY from TTYPath=.
StandardError.journal: Write to the journal (default), tagged with the unit metadata.
StandardError.kmsg: Write to the kernel log buffer (/dev/kmsg).
StandardError.kmsg+console: Kernel log buffer plus the console.
StandardError.fd: Write to a file descriptor passed to the manager.

TimeoutStartFailureMode.exit: Treat the timeout as a normal unclean exit.
TimeoutStartFailureMode.abort: Treat the timeout as a crash (core dump if enabled).
TimeoutStartFailureMode.kill: Kill the processes and mark the start failed (default).

TimeoutStopFailureMode.exit: Treat the timeout as a normal unclean exit.
TimeoutStopFailureMode.abort: Treat the timeout as a crash (core dump if enabled).
TimeoutStopFailureMode.kill: SIGKILL the processes and mark the stop failed (default).

KeyringMode.private: The unit gets its own session keyring (default).
KeyringMode.shared: The keyring is shared with the manager.
KeyringMode.inherit: Keep the keyring of the service manager.

ProtectProc.invisible: /proc entries of other processes are hidden.

ProcSubset.pid: Only own processes are visible in /proc (hidepid=2 equivalent).

ProtectSystem.strict: The whole hierarchy becomes read-only except /dev, /proc and /sys.

ProtectHome.tmpfs: Empty tmpfs are mounted over home directories.

DevicePolicy.closed: Access to standard devices like /dev/null, /dev/zero and /dev/random (default).
DevicePolicy.strict: Only devices listed in DeviceAllow= are accessible.
DevicePolicy.auto: Add accesses for all devices the unit opens at start (deprecated).

Personality.posix: Fallback when the architecture is unknown.

BindIPv6Only.default: Respect the kernel default for IPV6_V6ONLY.
BindIPv6Only.both: Bind to both IPv4 and IPv6 (V6ONLY off).

KillMode.control-group: All remaining processes in the control group are killed (default).
KillMode.process: Only the main process is killed.
KillMode.mixed: The main process gets SIGTERM; remaining processes get SIGKILL.
KillMode.user: All processes of the user are killed.

OOMPolicy.continue: Keep the scope running when the OOM killer strikes.
OOMPolicy.stop: Stop the scope when the OOM killer kills one of its processes.
OOMPolicy.kill: Kill all remaining processes of the cgroup (default for scopes).
